newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins dip in nervous trade, watch U.S..
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins dip in nervous trade, watch U.S..

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds eased in nervous trading on Tuesday following weaker Brady bonds, but dealers said MinFins found support later on short-covering.
They said future trends would depend mainly on the moves in Brady bonds and U.S. Treasuries.
"The day has been nervous as it started with selling following Monday's fall of emerging debt prices," an International Moscow Bank dealer said. "As a result, prices fell some 0.3 points."
Brady bond dealers attributed Monday's dip to uncertainty over an Argentine debt buyback and concerns about the spillover effect of Asian foreign exchange turmoil.
Dealers said the most actively traded MinFins, tranches 4 to 7, were finding support at 67.50, 49.50, 55.50 and 43.75, respectively.
They said the price decline stopped as traders closed short positions ahead of U.S. June retail sales data, which ended up only having a short-term impact on MinFins.

The U.S. Commerce Department said on Tuesday June retail sales rose 0.5 percent compared to a downwardly revised 0.3-percent decline in May. Economists in a Reuters survey had expected a 0.2-percent rise in sales.
Dealers said prices were little changed overall by the data, having steadied afterwards.
"The new figures are mixed for the market," Avtobank dealer Ivan Kuznetsov said. "There was brief selling, then buying after the data."
MinFins, along with other emerging market debt, are sensitive to any news suggesting a change in U.S. interest rates and U.S. Treasury bond prices.
